title: Constrained macrocycle series (illustrative)
objective: Hold a short peptide in a single conformation without losing the two residues that contact the target.
coordinate_note: Positions are 1-based within the chain. A sequence letter carries the monomer's natural analogue; where the chemistry differs, the chain's chemistry entry names the monomer at that position.

hypotheses.question: Does closing the backbone into a macrocycle improve affinity, rather than merely making the peptide rigid?
hypotheses.mechanism: The linear peptide pays a conformational entropy cost on binding. Removing the termini's freedom before binding should recover part of that cost, provided the bound conformation is still reachable once the ring is closed.
hypotheses.measurement: Affinity against the linear parent by the same binding assay, with a circular-dichroism spectrum to show the constraint took effect. A rigid peptide that binds no better separates the entropy account from rigidity on its own.

hypotheses.question: Is local backbone restriction in the tail enough, without closing the ring?
hypotheses.mechanism: A quaternary alpha-carbon narrows the backbone's accessible angles at one position only. If the entropy cost is concentrated in the tail, restricting it there should capture most of the gain at a fraction of the synthetic cost.
hypotheses.measurement: Affinity against both the linear parent and the macrocycle. Matching the macrocycle would locate the cost in the tail; matching the parent would place it elsewhere.

hypotheses.question: Does a single D-residue at the cleavage site extend half-life without changing the binding face?
hypotheses.mechanism: Proteases read backbone stereochemistry, so inverting one centre away from the contact residues should block cleavage while leaving the side chains that bind unchanged.
hypotheses.measurement: Serum half-life beside affinity. A gain in half-life with lost affinity would mean the inverted centre was not as far from the binding face as assumed.

caps.note: Amidated, which removes the C-terminal negative charge.

bonds.note: Closes the loop between positions 1 and 6. The record declares this bond; a pair of cysteines on its own would not establish that it forms.

residues.note: A quaternary alpha carbon with no alpha hydrogen.

variants.name: Head-to-tail cyclized
variants.headline: Closed backbone
variants.note: Same sequence as the parent. The backbone is closed head-to-tail, and the C-terminal amide is gone because the terminus it capped now carries that bond.

bonds.note: Head-to-tail closure, joining position 1 to position 9.

variants.headline: Inverted centre at the cleavage site
variants.note: Same letters as the parent, with D-alanine at position 8. The sequence alone describes the all-L peptide.

attempted_analyses.attempted: A search for a natural family to align against.
attempted_analyses.reason: This is a synthetic sequence with no natural homologs, so there is no ortholog set to align and no position can carry a conservation score. The track is absent because the comparison set does not exist.

precedent_search.scope: An illustrative fixture. No search was run, because the sequence is synthetic and exists only in this file.
precedent_search.reason: No prior art exists for this sequence. The record is an illustration of how non-canonical chemistry is represented.
